item.text: The loader writes before restoring calendar, language, and test fields, so a normal read can discard them. V2 migration also leaves credentials as an array. I’ll move persisted state into one config object and make initialization write only when migration or token creation changes it.

p='test/client/misc/DeviceConfigTest.ts'
s=open(p).read().replace('import {migrateConfig, migrateConfigV2to3}', 'import {DeviceConfig, migrateConfigV2to3}')
s=s.replace('const expectedCredentialsAfterMigration: Array<Omit<PersistentCredentials, \"databaseKey\">> = [','const expectedCredentialsAfterMigration: Record<string, Omit<PersistentCredentials, \"databaseKey\"> & {databaseKey: null}> = {\\n\\t\\t\\t\\tinternalUserId:')
s=s.replace('\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t},\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t{\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\tcredentialInfo:', '\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t},\\n\\t\\t\\t\\texternalUserId: {\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\tcredentialInfo:')
s=s.replace('encryptedPassword: \"internalEncPassword\"\\n', 'encryptedPassword: \"internalEncPassword\",\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\tdatabaseKey: null\\n').replace('encryptedPassword: \"externalEncPassword\",\\n', 'encryptedPassword: \"externalEncPassword\",\\n\\t\\t\\t\\t\\tdatabaseKey: null,\\n')
s=s.replace('''			]

			o(oldConfig._credentials)''','''			}

			o(oldConfig._credentials)''')
# append tests before last closing spec
idx=s.rfind('\\n})')
s=s[:idx]+'''
	o(\"loads current config without writing and retains every field\", function () {
		const stored = {
			_version: DeviceConfig.Version,
			_credentials: {user: {credentialInfo: {userId: \"user\", login: \"user@example.com\", type: \"internal\"}, accessToken: \"token\", encryptedPassword: \"password\", databaseKey: \"key\"}},
			_scheduledAlarmUsers: [\"user\"], _themeId: \"dark\", _language: \"en\",
			_defaultCalendarView: {user: \"month\"}, _hiddenCalendars: {user: [\"calendar\"]},
			_signupToken: \"existing\", _credentialEncryptionMode: null, _encryptedCredentialsKey: \"abc\",
			_testDeviceId: \"device\", _testAssignments: {assignment: \"value\"},
		}
		let writes = 0
		const storage = {
			getItem: () => JSON.stringify(stored),
			setItem: () => { writes++ },
		} as unknown as Storage
		const config = new DeviceConfig(DeviceConfig.Version, storage)
		o(writes).equals(0)
		o(config.loadByUserId(\"user\")?.databaseKey).equals(\"key\")
		o(config.getSignupToken()).equals(\"existing\")
		config.setTheme(\"light\")
		o(writes).equals(1)
	})

	o(\"migrates once and persists all fields under underscored keys\", function () {
		const stored: any = {
			_version: 2,
			_credentials: [{userId: \"user\", mailAddress: \"user@example.com\", accessToken: \"token\", encryptedPassword: \"password\"}],
			_scheduledAlarmUsers: [\"user\"], _themeId: \"dark\", _language: \"en\",
			_defaultCalendarView: {user: \"month\"}, _hiddenCalendars: {user: [\"calendar\"]},
			_signupToken: \"existing\", _credentialEncryptionMode: null, _encryptedCredentialsKey: \"abc\",
			_testDeviceId: \"device\", _testAssignments: {assignment: \"value\"},
		}
		let writes = 0
		let value = JSON.stringify(stored)
		const storage = {
			getItem: () => value,
			setItem: (_key: string, next: string) => { writes++; value = next },
		} as unknown as Storage
		new DeviceConfig(DeviceConfig.Version, storage)
		o(writes).equals(1)
		const saved = JSON.parse(value)
		o(saved._version).equals(DeviceConfig.Version)
		o(saved._credentials.user.credentialInfo.userId).equals(\"user\")
		for (const key of Object.keys(stored)) o(saved[key]).deepEquals(key === \"_credentials\" || key === \"_version\" ? saved[key] : stored[key])
		new DeviceConfig(DeviceConfig.Version, storage)
		o(writes).equals(1)
	})
''' +s[idx:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY"

item.text:
Updated [DeviceConfig.ts](/app/src/misc/DeviceConfig.ts) to keep persisted fields in one config object. Loading a current config with a signup token now makes no storage write; migration and missing-token generation write only after all fields are restored. V2 credentials migrate to an object keyed by user ID and load into a Map.

Added regression coverage in [DeviceConfigTest.ts](/app/test/client/misc/DeviceConfigTest.ts). Source and test type checks passed, and the client suite passed with 3,071 assertions.
